ai.description: *Dendrelaphis chairecacos* is a slender, medium-sized colubrid. It is bronze-brown dorsally with a distinct black lateral stripe and a pale, yellowish-white venter. It features a prominent black eye-stripe.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dendrelaphis chairecacos* is best distinguished by its distinct, broad black stripe running through the eye and along the neck, which lacks the white border seen in many similar *Dendrelaphis* species.
ai.habitat: *Dendrelaphis chairecacos* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests within the Western Ghats, typically found in low-to-mid-altitude vegetation and riparian zones.
ai.behavior: *Dendrelaphis chairecacos* is a diurnal, arboreal hunter that actively pursues lizards and frogs through the forest canopy with remarkable speed and agility.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis chairecacos* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dendrelaphis chairecacos* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at low to moderate elevations.
